newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians order controls to foil Jewish settlers.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians order controls to foil Jewish settlers.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority said on Saturday it had banned the sale of land through unauthorised agents in order to counter expansion of Jewish settlement.
The ban, affecting all of the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, covers areas now beyond Authority control, including Arab East Jerusalem which is part of the West Bank but is claimed by Israel.
The Authority's intention to enforce the ban in areas outside its control -- with a threat of unspecified punishment -- is sure to anger Israel.
The ban came days before U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross is to return to seek a way to resume peacemaking.

"In some cases where Israelis build new settlements on Palestinian land, we discovered that Palestinian owners have sold their land to Arab or foreign dealers working for Israeli companies," a PLO official told Reuters.
"To stop this, we are prohibiting the sales of land through (unauthorised) Arab or foreign dealers," he said of the decision taken at an Authority cabinet meeting overnight.
General Secretary of the Palestinian Authority, Ahmed Abdel-Rahman, said the Palestinian Authority would need to approve all land deals and all real estate agents.

"The leadership has ordered its security and judicial apparatus to see that the decision is implemented, and to punish anyone charged with (unauthorised) selling of land, whether directly or by facilitating the sale process, which is considered the greatest danger threatening Palestinian land," the Palestinian Authority statement said.

Peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians ground to a halt and violence erupted after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government sent bulldozers to begin a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18.

Palestinians, who want an independent state in the West Bank and Gaza Strip with East Jeruslem as its capital, view all Jewish settlement on lands captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war as pre-empting final status peace talks.
The final peace talks, which according to a framework peace deal are to end by mid-1999, have not resumed since the rightwing Netanyahu who took office in June.
